messages:
maria: FYI seeing a regression on canary after the bank-reshard merge (ae3b2f4). p95 decode for small-chat workloads jumped ~22% compared to previous canary. rolling hold on rollout.

derek: ugh, saw the spike in dashboards this morning. looks like short sequence paths are getting routed to a different attention kernel more often.

sasha: dug into traces — kv cache warmups look fine, but there's a lot of extra memcpy activity when requests cross bank boundaries. appears related to the new 'bank split' layout.

maria: attaching quick numbers: baseline (before): p50=38ms p95=198ms; after ae3b2f4: p50=44ms p95=241ms. qps same.

jen: CI perf-run flagged a 15% slowdown on decode microbench for shortseq too, job  #2286. gist: https://ci/redwood/2286 (private). ci-bot: @here perf test failed threshold.

ci-bot: PERF CHECK — job 2286: shortseq-decode p95 +15% vs baseline, failing gate.

will: quick profiler snapshot from canary box (nvprof-like sampling):
```
Sampling profile (top kernels):
attn_v1_main        42% -> 38%
attn_v2_star        12% -> 28%   <-- increased
kv_memcopy          8%  -> 14%   <-- extra copies when bank boundary crossed
matmul_fast         20% -> 18%
```

derek: attn_v2_star has a slightly different blocking/tiling; it benefits larger contiguous banks but is worse when the bank stride changes mid-request. the reshaping in ae3b2f4 changed bank stride heuristics.

sasha: confirmed with local run: forcing kernel selector to prefer attn_v1_main drops p95 back near baseline.

kevin: does the bank reshuffle change KV layout so that some cached KV pages need re-packing on append? that would explain the memcpy spike.

sasha: yes — bank-reshard introduced bank boundary alignment for quantized caches; when a request extends across an alignment we do an extra copy to coalesce. cheap for long sequences, expensive for many short sequences.

maria: notes: this repo change was intended to help throughput for long-run chat, but our canary traffic is mixed and dominated by lots of short interactions. bad regression surface.

jen: can we gate the heuristic by workload mix? or fallback to old behavior for shortseqs?

will: temp mitigation: runtime flag to disable bank splitting (ATTN_BANK_SPLIT=0) available in config. ran quick canary with flag set -> p95 back down to 202ms.

maria: good. can we ship a hotfix revert? what's minimal revert?

derek: smallest fix: change kernel selector scoring so attn_v2_star isn't chosen for sequences < 64 tokens or when kv-append crosses last-bank boundary. I'll draft a patch.

kevin: alternative is to skip coalescing memcpy when resulting range < 128 bytes and instead do an incremental append. might be simpler.

jen: ops asks: do we need to rollback deploy or hold canary? I've already put rollout on hold. deploy-bot: hold placed at 6154321200 by jen.

deploy-bot: rollout hold applied (canary target id: canary-7d).

maria: plan: 1) keep rollout hold, 2) flip ATTN_BANK_SPLIT=0 on canary cluster to buy time, 3) land derek's selector-scoring patch + test, 4) run perf jobs across shortseq and longseq mixes, 5) unhold when green.

will: I'll flip the flag on canary now and run 1k shortseq synthetic tests.

will: quick update — synthetic run: p95 returned to 205ms, memory churn down 60% on memcpy counters.

derek: I'll open a PR with the selector guard and include a microbench harness. requesting review from sasha/kevin.

sasha: if we go with the selector guard we should also add a debug metric to surface how often a request crosses bank boundary and triggers coalesce — helps detect future regressions.

maria: agreed. include metric and a small dashboard tile. also add a note to release notes that bank-reshard impacts shortseq.

jen: CI perf gate will re-run automatically after PR merges; keep an eye on job 2294. ci-bot will ping.

ci-bot: Perf job queued: 2294 (shortseq + mixed workload).

maria: thanks all. next updates here — if anyone sees anomalies on other canaries ping me directly. :thumbsup:
